actors.name: USCIS intake (online account / lockbox / National Benefits Center)
Designated USCIS investigator (neighborhood investigation under INA 335(a))
FBI Enterprise Vetting Center (formerly the National Name Check Program)
USCIS field office scheduling and clerical operations
Adjudicating immigration services officer (conducts the examination and decides)
Re-verification officer (quality review; not the interviewing officer)
Official with delegated Oath authority (Field Office Director or re-delegate; or a judge in a judicial ceremony)

activities.name: Self-screen eligibility: 18 or older, permanent resident for at least 5 years (or 3 years if married to a U.S. citizen), or a military basis

evidence.quote: In general, you may qualify for naturalization if you are at least 18 years old and have been a permanent resident for at least 5 years (or 3 years if you are married to a U.S. citizen)
evidence.page_or_section: Step 2, Determine your eligibility to become a U.S. citizen

activities.name: Prepare and sign Form N-400, collect the eligibility documents, and add Form N-648 if claiming a medical disability exception
artifacts_in: 2 passport-style photos if residing outside the U.S.

evidence.quote: Complete and sign your Form N-400. Get 2 passport-style photos taken if you reside outside the United States. Collect the necessary documents to demonstrate your eligibility for naturalization.
USCIS may ask for additional information if your application is incomplete. This will delay the processing of your application.

activities.name: File the N-400 online or on paper and pay the fee: $760 by paper, $710 online, $380 reduced fee, or request a fee waiver (fee-reduction and waiver requests cannot be filed online)

fee.when: at filing; $710 if filed online, $380 reduced fee, or $0 with an approved fee waiver

evidence.quote: Submit $760 if filing by paper, or $710 if filing online
You cannot file online if you are requesting a fee waiver or a reduced fee; you must file a paper Form N-400.

activities.name: Reject an unsigned filing or one without the correct fee, returning the application and any fees with an explanation

rework.reason: application unsigned or accompanied by the wrong fee

evidence.quote: USCIS will reject any Form N-400 that is not signed or accompanied by the correct filing fee.

activities.name: Issue the receipt notice, after which the applicant can track case status and published processing times

timing.source: user-report tier only (reddit timelines: same day to about a week for online filings). USCIS publishes no receipt-notice service level.

evidence.quote: Once you submit Form N-400 and get a receipt notice, you can check current processing times and the status of your application by visiting uscis.gov.

activities.name: Collect biometrics (fingerprints, photograph, signature) at an Application Support Center — or issue a notice that prior biometrics have been re-used
artifacts_in: biometrics appointment notice or biometrics-reuse notice

timing.source: user-report tier only (reddit: 4–28 days from receipt; many applicants now get a reuse notice the same day as the receipt notice). No official figure published.

fee.when: biometric services fee is included in the N-400 fee for most applicants

evidence.quote: USCIS must collect biometrics (fingerprints, photograph, signature) as part of the background check process on aliens applying for naturalization regardless of their age.
You will either receive a notice that your biometrics have been re-used, or, if new biometrics are required, you will receive a notice of a biometrics appointment.
evidence.page_or_section: Step 5, Go to the biometrics appointment

activities.name: Request FBI name checks through the FBI's Enterprise Vetting Center against the Universal Index, plus other security checks as necessary
artifacts_out: other security-check results in the record

timing.source: not published. 8 CFR 335.2(b) makes a 'definitive response' the gate on interview scheduling but attaches no service level to it.

evidence.quote: USCIS requests FBI “name checks” on all aliens applying for naturalization and receives the information contained in the FBI’s files in response to the name check requests.
The FBI’s Enterprise Vetting Center (EVC), formerly the National Name Check Program (NNCP) includes a search against the FBI’s Universal Index (UNI)

activities.name: Conduct the neighborhood investigation under INA 335(a): witness interviews in the vicinity of the applicant's residences and employment or business, covering at least the 5 years before filing, generally completed before the interview is scheduled
artifacts_in: witness testimony from neighbors, landlords, employers, coworkers, clients
artifacts_out: investigation results incorporated into the record

evidence.quote: Unless waived, the neighborhood investigation applies to all aliens and will generally be conducted and completed before the alien is scheduled for his or her naturalization interview.

Neighborhood investigations may include taking witness statements and testimonials in the vicinity of the alien’s: Residences; and either Employment; or Business’s location or self-employment location.

activities.name: Submit at least two character reference letters from U.S. citizens who personally know the applicant, which can support a waiver of the neighborhood investigation

evidence.quote: Proactively submitting at least two letters with the Application for Naturalization (Form N-400) can assist USCIS in determining whether a waiver of the neighborhood investigation is appropriate or not.
evidence.page_or_section: A.4, Decision to Require or Discretion to Waive a Neighborhood Investigation

evidence.quote: USCIS does not consider letters written by the alien’s immediate family or relatives.
evidence.page_or_section: A.4, Testimonial or Character Reference Letters

activities.name: Weigh the investigation record: decide discretionarily whether to waive the neighborhood investigation, and give the applicant notice of any derogatory information it produced plus an opportunity to refute it before denying on that basis
artifacts_in: character letters and other record evidence
artifacts_out: notice of the derogatory information and the applicant's rebuttal

evidence.quote: An alien’s failure or refusal to provide the letters may contribute to a decision to conduct a neighborhood investigation.
evidence.page_or_section: A.4, Decision to Require or Discretion to Waive

evidence.quote: USCIS may waive the neighborhood investigation if, using its discretion, USCIS determines that the waiver of the investigation is appropriate in a particular case or classes of cases.

If USCIS intends to deny the application based on derogatory information obtained from the investigation, USCIS must give the alien sufficient notice of the information and an opportunity to refute the adverse information.

activities.name: Schedule the examination and mail the interview appointment notice — but only after a definitive FBI response that the full criminal background check is complete. This is where the queue lives.

timing.source: observed (third-party scrape of the official API) — D13, as of Aug 17 2026: source-row average 11.5–14.8 months; full per-office range 8.0–26.0 months. Per-office values in timing_gold.per_office.

evidence.quote: USCIS will notify applicants for naturalization to appear before a USCIS officer for initial examination on the naturalization application only after the USCIS has received a definitive response from the Federal Bureau of Investigation
All applicants must have background checks completed before USCIS will schedule an interview.
evidence.page_or_section: Step 5, Go to the biometrics appointment

activities.name: Officer's pre-interview review of the A-file: build the issue list, verify the background and security checks were conducted and remain valid at adjudication, and check the record and relevant databases for a pending removal proceeding or prior final removal order (the INA 318 bar)
artifacts_in: A-file (prior benefit filings, correspondence, criminal records, investigative reports, enforcement actions)
Notice to Appear, Order to Show Cause, or final removal order if present

evidence.quote: A USCIS officer who is designated to conduct the naturalization interview should review the alien’s “A-file” and naturalization application before the interview.

An officer must ensure that all of the appropriate background and security checks have been conducted on the alien applying for naturalization and that the results of those checks remain valid at time of adjudication.
evidence.page_or_section: B.3, Results of Background and Security Checks

evidence.quote: An officer reviews an alien’s record and relevant databases to identify any current removal proceedings or previous proceedings resulting in a final order of removal from the United States.
evidence.page_or_section: B.4, Previous Notice to Appear, Order to Show Cause, or Removal Order

evidence.quote: USCIS cannot consider the naturalization application of an applicant who is in removal proceedings.

activities.name: Transfer the application to the office with jurisdiction if the applicant moved after filing; the applicant then gets a new appointment notice from the new office

rework.reason: jurisdiction changed; the receiving office reschedules the examination

evidence.quote: The officer informs the alien that the application’s jurisdiction has changed. The alien will receive a new appointment notice from the current office with jurisdiction.
You must notify USCIS if you change your address after filing your Form N-400 within 10 days of your relocation.

activities.name: Appear in person for the examination: the officer places the applicant under oath and questions them on every naturalization requirement and on any derogatory information from the investigation
artifacts_in: interpreter's oath and privacy release if an interpreter is used
artifacts_out: amendments to the application made in the course of the interview

evidence.quote: All aliens applying for naturalization must appear for an in-person examination before a USCIS officer after filing an Application for Naturalization (Form N-400).
The officer places the alien under oath and interviews the alien on the questions and responses in the alien’s naturalization application.

activities.name: Administer the English (speaking, reading, writing) and civics tests unless exempt — the 2008 test (up to 10 of 100 questions, 6 to pass) for pre-Oct 20 2025 filings, the 2025 test (20 of 128 questions, 12 to pass) for filings on or after that date

evidence.quote: The 2025 naturalization civics test is an oral test consisting of 20 questions from the list of 128 civics test questions. You must answer 12 questions correctly to pass the 2025 test.

In most cases, the officer conducting the naturalization interview administers the required tests relating to the alien’s ability to read and write English, and his or her knowledge of U.S. history and government (civics), unless the alien is exempt.

activities.name: Issue the notice of examination results (Form N-652) at the end of the examination regardless of the outcome, stating the next steps for a continued case
artifacts_out: Form N-652, Notice of Examination Results

evidence.quote: The officer must provide the applicant with a notice of results at the end of the interview regardless of the outcome. The notice should address the outcome of the interview and the next steps involved for continued cases.
USCIS will provide you with a notice of interview results following your interview.

activities.name: Continue the case with a written Request for Evidence (Form N-14); the applicant generally has 30 days to respond, and failure to respond lets the officer adjudicate on the available evidence

timing.source: designed — 8 CFR 335.7 (30 days, plus 3 days when mailed under 8 CFR 103.8(b))

rework.reason: additional documents or evidence needed before a decision can be made

evidence.quote: An officer issues the applicant a written Request for Evidence if additional information is needed to make an accurate determination on the naturalization application.
In general, USCIS permits a period of 30 days for the applicant to respond to a Request for Evidence.

activities.name: Schedule one re-examination between 60 and 90 days after the initial examination if the applicant failed a test component — retesting only the failed portion, still inside the 120-day window; a second failure means denial

timing.source: designed — 8 CFR 312.5(a) and 8 CFR 335.3(b) (not earlier than 60 days, scheduled within the 120-day window)

rework.reason: failed a portion of the naturalization test, or an eligibility issue needs resolving

evidence.quote: If an applicant fails any portion of the naturalization test, an officer must provide the applicant a second opportunity to pass the test within 60 to 90 days after the initial examination

If you fail any of the tests at your initial interview, you will be retested on the portion of the test that you failed (English or civics) between 60 and 90 days from the date of your initial interview.

activities.name: Decide within 120 days of the initial examination — approve, continue, or deny; miss the 120 days and the applicant may take the case to district court
artifacts_in: complete record including test results and any RFE response

timing.source: designed — 8 CFR 335.3(a) and 8 U.S.C. §1447(b) (120 days from the initial examination). Frequently exceeded per user reports; no official distribution of interview-to-decision times is published.

evidence.quote: USCIS has 120 days from the date of the initial naturalization interview to issue a decision. If the decision is not issued within 120 days of the interview, an applicant may request judicial review

A decision to grant or deny the application shall be made at the time of the initial examination or within 120-days after the date of the initial examination of the applicant for naturalization under § 335.2.

activities.name: Run every approved application through internal re-verification quality review by an officer who is not the interviewing officer, who may raise substantive eligibility issues without re-adjudicating
artifacts_out: re-verified approval, or an eligibility issue raised

rework.reason: re-verification officer raises a substantive eligibility issue

evidence.quote: The internal procedures include a “re-verification” procedure where all approved applications are reviewed for quality. The officer who conducts the re-verification is not the same officer who conducts the interview.
While the officer conducting the re-verification process does not adjudicate the application once again, the officer may raise any substantive eligibility issues.

activities.name: Deny in writing no later than 120 days after the initial interview, with a clear statement of the supporting facts, the specific eligibility requirements not met, and how to request a hearing

evidence.quote: If an officer denies a naturalization application, the officer must issue the applicant and his or her attorney or representative a written denial notice no later than 120 days after the initial interview on the application.
You will receive a notice from USCIS explaining the reason for your Form N-400 denial.

activities.name: Request a hearing on the denial by filing Form N-336 with the fee within 30 days of the decision date; miss it and the denial is final
artifacts_out: administrative hearing before an immigration officer

timing.source: designed — filing deadline only; no published decision time for the N-336 hearing

fee.when: N-336 filing fee, per Form G-1055

evidence.quote: You MUST file Form N-336 with the appropriate fee within 30 days of the Form N-400 decision date. If a request for hearing is not filed within the time allowed, the denial decision is final.

activities.name: Treat a failure to appear as abandonment: a missed fingerprinting appointment without good cause, or a missed initial examination not explained within 30 days, lets USCIS administratively close the application without a merits decision; reopening is free within 1 year, after which it is dismissed without notice
artifacts_in: missed biometrics appointment or missed initial examination
artifacts_out: or reopening (the reopening date becomes the new filing date)

fee.when: reopening within 1 year carries no additional fee

rework.reason: application reopened; the examination must be rescheduled

evidence.quote: An alien abandons his or her naturalization application if the applicant fails to appear for the fingerprinting appointment without good cause and without notifying USCIS.

An applicant abandons their application if the applicant fails to appear for their initial naturalization examination without good cause and without notifying USCIS of the reason for non-appearance within 30 days of the scheduled appointment.
evidence.page_or_section: D.1, Administrative Closure for Failing to Appear

evidence.quote: An applicant may reopen an administratively closed application by submitting a written request to USCIS within one (1) year from the date the application was closed. Such reopening shall be without additional fee.

activities.name: Identify post-approval disqualifying derogatory information and pull the applicant's name off every list of granted applications and of applicants scheduled for the oath — the oath must not be scheduled or administered until the matter resolves favorably
artifacts_in: derogatory information received or identified after approval
artifacts_out: name removed from the oath list

evidence.quote: USCIS must not schedule an applicant for the administration of the Oath of Allegiance if USCIS receives or identifies disqualifying derogatory information. USCIS must not administer the Oath of Allegiance to the applicant until the matter is resolved favorably.
evidence.page_or_section: B, Derogatory Information Received before Oath or Failure to Appear

evidence.quote: USCIS shall remove the applicant's name from any list of granted applications or of applicants scheduled for administration of the oath of allegiance, until such time as the matter can be resolved.

activities.name: Execute a motion to reopen the already-granted application, giving the applicant 15 days to overcome the derogatory information or show good cause for missing ceremonies; otherwise the motion is granted and the application is denied on the merits
artifacts_in: derogatory information, or two or more missed oath ceremonies
artifacts_out: re-approval and oath scheduling, or denial

evidence.quote: The applicant has 15 days to respond to the motion to reopen and overcome the derogatory information or provide good cause for failing to appear at the Oath ceremony.
evidence.page_or_section: B, Derogatory Information Received before Oath

evidence.quote: If the applicant is unable to overcome the derogatory information, the officer grants the motion to reopen and denies the application on its merits.

activities.name: Schedule the oath ceremony and mail Form N-445, Notice of Naturalization Oath Ceremony, with the date, time and location; a few offices run daily ceremonies where examination, adjudication and oath happen the same day

timing.source: no regulatory clock and no published figure for approval-to-oath. User reports in this corpus span 2 days to 9.5+ weeks, with cancelled-and-unrescheduled cases running 7+ months.

evidence.quote: If a ceremony is unavailable, we will mail you a notice with the date, time, and location of your scheduled naturalization ceremony on Form N-445, Notice of Naturalization Oath Ceremony.
evidence.page_or_section: What to Expect, 1. Receive a Notice to Take the Oath of Allegiance

evidence.quote: In some instances, USCIS offices may conduct daily ceremonies where the examination, adjudication, and the oath take place on the same day.

activities.name: Check in at the ceremony, have a USCIS officer review the completed Form N-445 questionnaire responses, and surrender the Permanent Resident Card

evidence.quote: A USCIS officer will review your responses to the questionnaire, Form N-445, Notice of Naturalization Oath Ceremony.
evidence.page_or_section: What to Expect, 2. Check in at the Ceremony

evidence.quote: You must return your Permanent Resident Card to USCIS when you check in for your naturalization ceremony.
evidence.page_or_section: What to Expect, 3. Return your Permanent Resident Card

activities.name: Take the Oath of Allegiance in English at a public ceremony before an official with delegated Oath authority (or a judge in a judicial ceremony), then receive the Certificate of Naturalization and review it before leaving the site
artifacts_in: interpreter if the applicant brings one
artifacts_out: administered Oath of Allegiance; the applicant becomes a citizen

evidence.quote: The Oath of Allegiance is administered in the English language, regardless of whether the applicant was eligible for an exception to the English language requirements.
During judicial naturalization ceremonies, the judge in the district of proper jurisdiction has exclusive authority to administer the Oath.
evidence.page_or_section: B, Authority to Administer the Oath

evidence.quote: You are not a U.S. citizen until you take the Oath of Allegiance at a naturalization ceremony.
evidence.page_or_section: What to Expect, 4. Take the Oath of Allegiance

evidence.quote: Carefully review your Certificate of Naturalization and notify USCIS of any errors before leaving the ceremony.
evidence.page_or_section: What to Expect, 5. Receive Certificate of Naturalization

evidence.quote: Receive your Certificate of Naturalization and review it before leaving the ceremony site. Notify USCIS of any corrections to your certificate at that time.
evidence.page_or_section: Step 9, Take the Oath of Allegiance

activities.name: Presume abandonment when the applicant fails to appear for more than one oath ceremony, treating it as equivalent to post-approval derogatory information
artifacts_out: motion to reopen; denial if unanswered within 15 days

rework.reason: failure to appear for at least two oath ceremonies without good cause

evidence.quote: USCIS presumes an applicant to have abandoned his or her naturalization application when the applicant fails to appear for more than one oath ceremony.
USCIS considers multiple failures to appear to be equivalent to receipt of derogatory information after the approval of a naturalization application.

activities.name: Petition the U.S. district court: for a decision when USCIS has not decided within 120 days of the examination, or for de novo review of a denial after the N-336 hearing
artifacts_in: examination held more than 120 days ago with no decision, or a final administrative denial
artifacts_out: court determination or remand with instructions

timing.source: not published; no timed instance in this corpus

rework.reason: court orders USCIS to decide, or remands with instructions

evidence.quote: If the decision is not issued within 120 days of the interview, an applicant may request judicial review of his or her application in district court.

timing_gold.source: observed, third-party scrape of the official USCIS processing-times API — D13 (ImmigrationTimes.org, as of Aug 17 2026). The primary API at egov.uscis.gov/processing-times/ was Cloudflare-blocked (HTTP 403) to this session, so the aggregator is used and labelled as secondary/derived. Per-office case counts come from the primary official dataset, D12.
timing_gold.quote: As of Aug 17, 2026, USCIS processing times for N-400 (Application for Naturalization) range from 8.0 mo to 26.0 mo across all field offices (full range; source-row average 11.5 mo–14.8 mo).
timing_gold.caveat: USCIS publishes a RANGE per office, not a median and a p90: the lower bound is roughly a median-of-completions figure and the upper bound is the time within which about 80% of cases complete. 350 and 451 days are the national source-row average bounds (11.5 and 14.8 months) converted at 30.44 days/month. They are NOT a true median and p90 and must not be scored as if they were.
timing_gold.note: Field-office codes are counter-intuitive and worth preserving: San Francisco is SFR (not SFO), San Jose is SNJ, Santa Ana is SAA. The per-office approval counts are startling next to the pending counts — San Jose approved 314 while holding 20,860 pending in the same window, versus New York's 2,311 approvals against 17,028 pending. Throughput, not intake, is what separates these offices.

known_gaps: The FBI 'definitive response' service level. 8 CFR 335.2(b) makes it the gate on the single longest wait in the process (A13), and nothing in the regulation, the Policy Manual, or any statistic quantifies how long it takes or how often it stalls.

Why any specific case is continued a second time rather than approved or denied. The Policy Manual gives the officer's full menu (approve / continue with N-14 / re-examine / deny) but no selection logic, and no distribution of interview-to-decision times is published — so the 120-day rule's real compliance rate is unknown.

Approval-to-oath scheduling. There is no regulatory clock at all between A23 and A29, and no published figure. The only mechanism the documents describe for a cancelled or unscheduled oath is the derogatory-information motion to reopen (A27/A28); user reports in this corpus include a ceremony cancelled with no reason given and still unscheduled 7+ months later, which that mechanism does not obviously explain.

Per-office queue discipline: which filing cohorts an office works, and in what order. The FY2026 Q3 data shows San Jose approving 314 cases against 20,860 pending in the same window, but nothing published explains the throughput difference between offices.

Biometrics reuse. The decision to reuse prior fingerprints rather than schedule an appointment (A06) is stated as a possibility on the applicant-facing brochure but no document collected gives the criteria, and it materially changes the front of the timeline.

Combination adjudication. An I-751 pending in parallel appears in practice to gate N-400 approval, and combined I-751 + N-400 interviews are routine, but no document in the declared or designed tier describes either practice.

Nationality- or country-based pauses on interviews and oath ceremonies. A real, dated administrative pause affecting applicants from a list of countries is visible only through affected applicants' reports; no USCIS policy page collected acknowledges it.

No current oversight report. The CIS Ombudsman page is now a stub that links no annual report at all; the most recent report recoverable was 2023 (via the Wayback Machine), and no GAO or OIG naturalization-backlog report was located.

USCIS's own processing-times API is Cloudflare-blocked, so the per-office numbers in this gold file pass through a third-party aggregator. The case counts (D12) are primary; the month ranges (D13) are not.
notes: One model, five timing variants: the process shape is federal and uniform, and the only thing that varies by implementer is throughput, so per-office data lives in timing_gold.per_office rather than in separate models. Visibility calls were checked against the applicant-facing documents held in raw/: the background-check-before-interview gate, biometrics reuse, the continuation/N-14 path, the 60–90-day retest, the N-336 appeal and the whole ceremony sequence are all stated in D7 (M-1051), D8, D9 or D10, so they are marked applicant_facing even though their operational detail comes from the Policy Manual. Eight activities appear in no applicant-facing document held here and are marked staff_only: the FBI name check mechanics (A08), the neighborhood investigation (A09), the character-letter path and the waiver/derogatory-information weighing that follows it (A10, A11), the A-file pre-review including the INA 318 removal-proceedings database check (A14), the internal re-verification quality review of every approval (A23), the removal of a name from the oath list on post-approval derogatory information (A27), and the two-missed-ceremonies abandonment presumption (A33). A09 and A23 are the two a solver working only from the declared tier could not reach by any route: the neighborhood investigation is a physical visit to the applicant's neighbours and employer that no applicant-facing USCIS page mentions, and the re-verification step means every approval is silently reviewed by a second officer. Note also that A10 is a rare case of an applicant-facing ACTION whose purpose is staff_only: the brochures never mention character reference letters, so an applicant cannot know that sending two of them may spare them a neighbourhood investigation. Sibling-process contamination to guard against in scoring: I-130/I-485 adjustment-of-status timelines and I-751 conditional-residence removal both appear constantly in the same user-report corpus and share the receipt/biometrics/interview vocabulary; neither is part of this model.
